title: Universal root coordinates and normalizer relators in semisimple rank at most two
statement:
Let $A$ be a nonzero commutative ring and $P=(G,T=D_A(M),\Phi,\Phi^\vee,\Delta,(X_\alpha))$ a pinned split realization [def-sfb-pinned-split-root-realization], with $|\Delta|\leq2$. Write $\mathbf G_a(R)=(R,+)$ and $\mathbf G_m(R)=R^\times$ for every commutative $A$-algebra $R$. For every root $\gamma$ and every generator $Y$ of its tangent root module there is a unique $T$-equivariant closed group homomorphism $x_{\gamma,Y}:\mathbf G_a\to G$ whose differential sends $1$ to $Y$, where $t\in T(R)$ acts on $R$ by multiplication by the full character $\gamma(t)$. Write $U_\gamma$ for its image, independent of $Y$.

For each simple root $\alpha$, the pinning determines an opposite generator $X_{-\alpha}$ such that there is a homomorphism $v_\alpha:\operatorname{SL}_{2,A}\to G$ carrying $I+zE_{12}$ to $x_\alpha(z)=x_{\alpha,X_\alpha}(z)$, $I+zE_{21}$ to $x_{-\alpha}(z)=x_{-\alpha,X_{-\alpha}}(z)$, and $\operatorname{diag}(z,z^{-1})$ to $\alpha^\vee(z)$. Here $\operatorname{SL}_{2,A}(R)$ consists of determinant-one $2$ by $2$ matrices and $E_{ij}$ is the elementary matrix. Put $n_\alpha=x_\alpha(1)x_{-\alpha}(-1)x_\alpha(1)$. It normalizes $T$, acts on its character lattice by $s_\alpha(m)=m-\langle m,\alpha^\vee\rangle\alpha$, and satisfies
$$n_\alpha^2=\alpha^\vee(-1),\qquad(n_\alpha x_\alpha(1))^3=1.$$
The maps $x_{\pm\alpha}$ and $n_\alpha$ are unchanged under inclusion of the full-torus simple-root centralizer containing them in [lem-sfb-small-centralizer-hom-amalgamation].

Choose an enumeration of $\Delta$ (short root first when lengths differ). There is a choice, depending only on the enumerated abstract based root system, of a signed word in the $n_\alpha$ transporting a simple-root generator to a generator $X_\gamma$ of each positive-root module. It agrees with the given pinning at simple roots. Set $x_\gamma=x_{\gamma,X_\gamma}$. For every ordering of $\Phi^+$, multiplication identifies $\prod_{\gamma\in\Phi^+}\mathbf G_a$ with a closed subgroup $U^+\subseteq G$ by $(z_\gamma)\mapsto\prod_\gamma x_\gamma(z_\gamma)$. For distinct positive roots $\gamma,\eta$, in a fixed order on roots $i\gamma+j\eta$ with $i,j>0$, the interchange law has the form
$$x_\eta(y)x_\gamma(x)=x_\gamma(x)x_\eta(y)\prod_{i,j>0,\ i\gamma+j\eta\in\Phi}x_{i\gamma+j\eta}(C_{i,j,\gamma,\eta}x^iy^j),\qquad C_{i,j,\gamma,\eta}\in\mathbf Z.$$
For $\alpha\in\Delta$ and $\gamma\in\Phi^+\setminus\{\alpha\}$ there are signs $u_{\alpha,\gamma}\in\{1,-1\}$ with
$$n_\alpha x_\gamma(z)n_\alpha^{-1}=x_{s_\alpha\gamma}(u_{\alpha,\gamma}z).$$
The constants $C$ and $u$ depend only on the enumerated abstract based root system, not on $A$, $M$, or the realization. In rank two, for the two distinct simple roots $\alpha,\beta$, let $m_{\alpha\beta}$ be the order of $s_\alpha s_\beta$. Then
$$(n_\alpha n_\beta)^{m_{\alpha\beta}}=\prod_{\gamma\in\Phi^+}\gamma^\vee(-1).$$
All assertions are scheme-theoretic, hold after arbitrary ring base change, and impose no characteristic or Noetherian hypothesis. In rank zero $U^+=1$ and all root-indexed assertions are empty.

source.place: Theorem 4.1.4 (canonical root groups), Theorem 4.2.6 (opposite-root pairing), Theorem 5.1.8 (rank-one structure), Corollary 5.1.9 and Remark 5.1.10 (rank-one Weyl representatives), Proposition 5.1.16 (positive ordered products), and Lemma 6.2.8 with Steps 2--4 of the Isogeny Theorem, printed pp.205--209 (universal rank-two constants). The last Weyl-word formula is an agent-explicit formulation of the normalizer relator (6.2.3) required in Step 4, using the coroot word for the square of a longest Weyl representative; it is not asserted to be a quotation of Lemma 6.2.8 Read online; local PDF WANTED. This is Conrad, Reductive Group Schemes, not an invocation of any SGA source. No Stacks tag states this group-theoretic input.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-split-root-subgroup-weyl-calculus] to $P$. Identify the additive group of $\mathfrak g_\gamma$ with $\mathbf G_a$ using $z\mapsto zY$. Composing with $\exp_\gamma$ gives $x_{\gamma,Y}$. Conversely any homomorphism in the statement precomposed with the inverse of this identification has tangent inclusion and is $T$-equivariant, so the cited uniqueness applies. If $Y'=cY$ for a unit $c$, the new map is $x_{\gamma,Y}(cz)$; hence its closed image is the same $U_\gamma$. Equivariance uses the full character, exactly as in the cited statement, and uniqueness remains true after any base change.

source.place: Theorem 4.1.4; change of basis in the free root line

proof.text: For a simple root $\alpha$, [lem-sfb-small-centralizer-hom-amalgamation] supplies the full-torus centralizer $H=G_{\{\alpha\}}$ with just the roots $\pm\alpha$ and the original coroot. Choose any negative root-line generator. Apply [lem-sfb-reductive-framed-noetherian-descent] to this framed rank-one group: it descends to a nonzero Noetherian subring $A_0$ with the same two free root lines. Choose a lattice basis for $M$ and apply [lem-sfb-relative-rank-one-local-matrix-model] over $A_0$. Pull its affine open cover and its matrix-pair isomorphisms back to $A$. On each resulting open $\operatorname{Spec}C$, $H$ is a central torus times $\operatorname{SL}_2$, $\operatorname{PGL}_2$ or $\operatorname{GL}_2$, and $\alpha$ is the ratio character. The positive vector is $cE_{12}$ for a unit $c\in C^\times$. Define a local map from $\operatorname{SL}_2$ by $g\mapsto\operatorname{diag}(c,1)g\operatorname{diag}(c^{-1},1)$ in the matrix factor, followed by the projective quotient if needed, and the identity point in the central torus.

The local maps in step 2 have upper and lower restrictions $z\mapsto I+czE_{12}$ and $z\mapsto I+c^{-1}zE_{21}$. The canonical-exponential uniqueness in [lem-sfb-split-root-subgroup-weyl-calculus] identifies their upper restrictions with $x_\alpha$ and their lower restrictions with the exponentials of $c^{-1}E_{21}$. The image of $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&1\\-1&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ normalizes the whole torus in each model. Thus its negative tangent vector is the unique linked vector of the same cited node; these negative vectors agree on overlaps. On the diagonal the local map is $z\mapsto\operatorname{diag}(z,z^{-1})$ in the matrix factor. On every geometric fibre this is the canonical coroot, hence the original $\alpha^\vee$. The geometric-fibre equality criterion for maps of split diagonalizable groups in [lem-sfb-relative-diagonalizable-character-duality] proves equality of these torus morphisms over the whole open, including nilpotents.

source.place: Corollary 5.1.9 and rank-one matrix models; equality of torus maps

proof.text: The local maps therefore agree on both elementary unipotents and on the diagonal. These restrictions determine a map out of $\operatorname{SL}_2$: for $g=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}p&q\\ r&s\end{smallmatrix}\right)$, on $D(p)$ one has $g=L(r/p)\operatorname{diag}(p,p^{-1})U(q/p)$. On $D(r)$ the same factorization applies to $w^{-1}g$, where $w=U(1)L(-1)U(1)$, since its upper-left entry is $-r$. The opens cover because $ps-qr=1$. Thus the local morphisms agree everywhere on overlaps. The open cover of the affine base is an etale covering, hence fpqc by [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-finer-than-etale]; its pullback to $\operatorname{SL}_2$ and to its square is fpqc by [lem-galois-fpqc-covering-base-change]. Use [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] to glue the maps and detect their multiplication equality on the square. This constructs $v_\alpha$ and its required three restrictions.

source.place: Theorem 5.1.8; explicit two-chart gluing of the rank-one homomorphism

proof.text: In $\operatorname{SL}_2$ one computes $w=U(1)L(-1)U(1)=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&1\\-1&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)$, $w^2=-I$, and $(wU(1))^3=I$. Applying $v_\alpha$ proves the two rank-one identities. The normalizer action, its reflection on $M$, and compatibility of the linked vector and $n_\alpha$ under the inclusions $G_{\{\alpha\}}\subseteq G$ are exactly the subgroup-compatibility assertions of [lem-sfb-split-root-subgroup-weyl-calculus], applied to the centralizers from [lem-sfb-small-centralizer-hom-amalgamation]. Hence all rank-one data here agree with the constructions in those centralizers.

source.place: Corollary 5.1.9 and Remark 5.1.10; explicit SL2 matrices

proof.text: In rank two take the four positive-root lists and the signed transport words of [lem-sfb-rank-two-root-string-seed-calculus]. They use only the enumerated abstract root system; each transported vector is in the specified root module and is a generator, since conjugation by a normalizer element is an isomorphism of root modules. In rank one retain its given positive simple vector. The assertion of [lem-sfb-split-root-subgroup-weyl-calculus] for a closed subset $\Psi$ applies to $\Psi=\Phi^+$: a sum of positive roots which is a root remains positive. It proves the multiplication isomorphism onto a closed subgroup, in every ordering, with image independent of the ordering. Using $z\mapsto zX_\gamma$ gives the claimed affine coordinates on $U^+$.

We will use the following elementary weight comparison. If independent roots $r,s$ have no root $ir+js$ with $i,j>0$, their set is closed. The product-coordinate theorem of [lem-sfb-split-root-subgroup-weyl-calculus] puts $x_s(y)x_r(x)$ in $U_{\{r,s\}}$, with polynomial coordinates $F(x,y),H(x,y)$. Torus equivariance makes their monomials have respective weights $r,s$ in $A[M][x,y]$. Independence of $r,s$ forces $F=cx$, $H=dy$; setting one variable zero gives $c=d=1$. Thus these root groups commute as schemes over every ring. This also applies to pairs with a negative root when the same no-positive-combination condition holds. It uses Laurent monomials $e^m$ as an $A$-basis, not differentiated weights, so remains valid in small characteristic and over nonreduced rings.

source.place: Proposition 5.1.16, two-root closed sets; explicit weight comparison

proof.text: Here are all the simple-reflection signs, derived from the transport words. Write $c,d,e,f$ as in step 6, and list only the positive roots different from the acting simple root. In $A_2$, the $n_a$ images of $(X_b,X_c)$ are $(-X_c,X_b)$, and the $n_b$ images of $(X_a,X_c)$ are $(X_c,-X_a)$. In $B_2$, the $n_a$ images of $(X_b,X_c,X_d)$ are $(X_d,-X_c,X_b)$, and the $n_b$ images of $(X_a,X_c,X_d)$ are $(X_c,-X_a,X_d)$. In $G_2$, the $n_a$ images of $(X_b,X_c,X_d,X_e,X_f)$ are $(-X_e,X_d,-X_c,X_b,X_f)$, and the $n_b$ images of $(X_a,X_c,X_d,X_e,X_f)$ are $(X_c,-X_a,X_d,X_f,-X_e)$. To verify these lists, the forward arrows are the defining words, the A2 cross arrow and B2 middle arrow are the two isolated tangent identities in [lem-sfb-rank-two-root-string-seed-calculus], and the reverse arrows follow from $n_i^2=i^\vee(-1)$ and its action $(-1)^{\langle r,i^\vee\rangle}$ on the $r$-root module from [lem-sfb-split-root-subgroup-weyl-calculus]. The fixed arrows for $(b,d)$ in B2 and G2 and $(a,f)$ in G2 follow from step 7 for both $\pm b,d$ or $\pm a,f$: each of the three factors of $n_i$ commutes with that root group. In $A_1\times A_1$, the same argument gives both signs $+1$. The unique exponential with a given tangent vector then turns each listed tangent equality into the asserted conjugation equality for all parameters.

source.place: Lemma 6.2.8 and Example 6.2.9; calculation of every conjugation sign

proof.text: Apply the simple-root interchange seeds of [lem-sfb-rank-two-root-string-seed-calculus]. The root lists there show that every unordered positive pair admitting a positive combination root is a listed seed, except $(c,d)$ in $G_2$. For that pair conjugate the seed $x_d(y)x_a(x)=x_a(x)x_d(y)x_e(kxy)$ by $n_b$. Step 8 sends $a,d,e$ to $c,d,f$, with sign $+1$ in each case, so it gives $x_d(y)x_c(x)=x_c(x)x_d(y)x_f(kxy)$ with the same integer $k$. Every other unordered pair commutes by step 7. Thus there is an integer interchange rule for every unordered pair. All transports just substitute signed parameters and move root labels by a reflection; they introduce neither division nor a choice depending on the realization.

source.place: Lemma 6.2.8 and Example 6.2.9; the remaining nonsimple pair

proof.text: For completeness this determines reversed orientations and arbitrary factor orders integrally. Assign to a positive root its height, the sum of its simple coefficients. Every correction factor in step 9 has height strictly larger than either input height. In a collecting calculation, swap adjacent inverted factors by a rule of step 9, combine equal root factors by $x_r(u)x_r(v)=x_r(u+v)$, and proceed in increasing height. At any fixed height there are finitely many root positions and swaps; new correction terms have strictly larger height, so the calculation terminates at the largest root height. The inverse coordinate change is solved in the same increasing-height order: its coordinate at height $h$ is the old one plus a polynomial in lower-height coordinates, so inversion only subtracts that polynomial. This supplies swaps in the reversed orientation as well. Applying these changes to the seed identities yields an ordered product with polynomial coefficients in $\mathbf Z[x,y]$ for any prescribed root order. The product is unique by [lem-sfb-split-root-subgroup-weyl-calculus]. Its coordinate at $i\gamma+j\eta$ has weight $i\gamma+j\eta$, hence is a single integer multiple of $x^iy^j$ by the Laurent-monomial comparison of step 7; both inputs are independent positive roots. Vanishing on $x=0$ and $y=0$ excludes $i=0$ or $j=0$ from correction factors. This proves the precise form of every $C$ and its universality.

source.place: Proposition 5.1.16 and Lemma 6.2.8; integral triangular collection

proof.text:
Let $m=m_{ab}$ in rank two, and let $Q=A_m$ be the alternating word in $n_a,n_b$ starting with $n_a$. By [lem-sfb-rank-two-pinned-braid], $A_m=B_m$. Reversing $Q$ gives $B_m$ if $m$ is even and $A_m$ if $m$ is odd, so $Q^{\mathrm{rev}}=Q$. Also $(n_an_b)^m=Q^2$: for even $m$ this is the definition of $Q$, and for odd $m$ the product $A_mB_m$ is the alternating word of length $2m$ starting with $n_a$. Thus $(n_an_b)^m=Q Q^{\mathrm{rev}}$. Write $Q=q_1\cdots q_m$, with $q_j=n_{i_j}$. Cancel symmetrically from the middle, replacing $q_j^2$ by $i_j^\vee(-1)$ and conjugating it past the preceding $q_1\cdots q_{j-1}$. By the reflection action on the torus in [lem-sfb-split-root-subgroup-weyl-calculus], this gives
$$Q Q^{\mathrm{rev}}=\prod_{j=1}^m (s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_{j-1}}i_j)^\vee(-1).$$
The factors are in the commutative torus, so their order is immaterial.

source.place: Normalizer relations (6.2.3); explicit symmetric cancellation of the braid word

proof.text: The root lists of [lem-sfb-rank-two-root-string-seed-calculus] check the last product without any further Weyl-group theorem. For the alternating word starting with $a$, the successive roots $s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_{j-1}}i_j$ are $(a,b)$ in $A_1\times A_1$, $(a,a+b,b)$ in $A_2$, $(a,2a+b,a+b,b)$ in $B_2$, and $(a,3a+b,2a+b,3a+2b,a+b,b)$ in $G_2$. These lists follow by substituting the respective Cartan pairs $(\langle b,a^\vee\rangle,\langle a,b^\vee\rangle)=(0,0),(-1,-1),(-2,-1),(-3,-1)$, into $s_i(r)=r-\langle r,i^\vee\rangle i$ (in nonsimply-laced types $\langle b,a^\vee\rangle=-2$ or $-3$ and $\langle a,b^\vee\rangle=-1$). In each case it is exactly $\Phi^+$ once. Here $m=m_{ab}$ is $2,3,4,6$ respectively: on $\operatorname{span}_{\mathbf Q}(a,b)$ the matrix of $s_as_b$ has determinant $1$ and trace $\langle b,a^\vee\rangle\langle a,b^\vee\rangle-2=-2,-1,0,1$, and $s_as_b$ is the identity on the common kernel of $a^\vee,b^\vee$ in $M\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Q$, a complement of that span because the Cartan matrix is invertible. Thus step 11 gives the claimed product of all positive coroots evaluated at $-1$. For the other order of the two simple roots, $(n_bn_a)^m=n_b(n_an_b)^mn_b^{-1}$ is the image of this torus element under $s_b$ by the reflection action of [lem-sfb-split-root-subgroup-weyl-calculus]; since $s_b$ permutes $\Phi^+\setminus\{b\}$ (the lists of step 8) and $(s_bb)^\vee(-1)=b^\vee(-1)^{-1}=b^\vee(-1)$, it is the same product.

source.place: Finite rank-two lists in Isogeny Theorem Step 2; explicit inversion-root enumeration

proof.text: For rank zero, [lem-sfb-split-root-subgroup-weyl-calculus] applied to the empty closed root set gives the identity subgroup as the empty product, and every indexed assertion is empty. In rank one there is one positive root, so there are no distinct-positive-root or rank-two-pair assertions; the remaining statements were proved in steps 1--6. For arbitrary base change, canonical exponentials and the linked normalizer data commute with it by the same cited node. The local matrix maps of steps 2--4, after pullback, agree with the new maps on the two unipotents and the diagonal and hence everywhere by the explicit two-chart uniqueness in step 4. Transport words, integer polynomial identities and the word cancellation in steps 6--12 pull back literally. All claims are therefore scheme-theoretic and compatible with arbitrary and successive base change. If the target ring is zero its base scheme is empty and all comparisons hold uniquely.
